questions.q: Land cover class (forest, water, developed) is measured at which level?
questions.why: The categories have no inherent order. Even NLCD's numeric codes are only labels.
The categories are ordered, but the distance between categories isn't consistent.

questions.q: Why is 80°F not "twice as hot" as 40°F?
options: Fahrenheit is interval: differences are meaningful, but there's no true zero
questions.why: 0°F doesn't mean an absence of temperature, so ratios aren't meaningful.

questions.q: Which of these is ratio data?
options: Survey response from strongly disagree to strongly agree
questions.why: Distance has a true zero, so it's meaningful to say one place is twice as far as another.

questions.q: Converting median household income into income categories...
options: makes the data easier to communicate but always loses information
turns ratio data into nominal data
questions.why: Moving to a lower level of measurement (ratio to ordinal) simplifies the data at the cost of detail.

questions.q: Why does the Census Bureau report median household income rather than the mean?
options: The median is easier to calculate
The median isn't affected by extreme values, and income is skewed
The mean can't be calculated for income
questions.why: A few very high incomes pull the mean upward. The median depends only on the order of the values.

questions.q: What is the only measure of central tendency you can use for nominal data?
questions.why: With unordered categories, you can only ask which category is most common.

questions.q: A variable's mean is much larger than its median. The distribution most likely...
options: has a long tail of high values (positive skew)
has a long tail of low values (negative skew)
questions.why: Extreme high values pull the mean above the median.

questions.q: Which measure of spread is resistant to outliers and pairs with the median?
questions.why: The IQR is the spread of the middle 50% (Q3 minus Q1). It's the box in a boxplot.

questions.q: Why are the differences from the mean squared when calculating the variance?
options: So positive and negative differences don't cancel each other out
To convert to the original units
questions.why: Without squaring, deviations above and below the mean would sum to zero. The square root then returns to the original units.

questions.q: You want to compare whether rainfall varies more in the NC mountains or on the coast, where average rainfall differs a lot. Which measure fits best?
questions.why: The CV divides the standard deviation by the mean, so variability is expressed as a percentage of the mean and can be compared.

questions.q: Life expectancy, where most places have high values and a few have much lower values, is likely...
questions.why: The long tail is on the low side, which pulls the mean below the median.

questions.q: A distribution with high kurtosis (leptokurtic) has...
options: a flatter peak and lighter tails than the normal distribution
a sharper peak and heavier tails, meaning more extreme values
the same shape as the normal distribution
questions.why: Kurtosis is about how much of the data is in the tails compared to a normal distribution.

questions.q: Why might you take the natural log of population density before an analysis?
options: To make a strongly skewed distribution more symmetric
To convert it to ordinal data
questions.why: Many methods assume roughly normal data or residuals, and a log transformation pulls in a long right tail.

questions.q: Going from NC zip codes to counties, which statistic changes the most for percent poverty?
options: The standard deviation and the range
questions.why: Aggregating averages out local variation. Central tendency stays fairly stable while dispersion and the min and max shrink. This is the scale effect of the MAUP.

questions.q: The mean income across census tracts treats a tract of 1,500 people the same as a tract of 8,000. To describe the typical person, you should use...
questions.why: Describing places and describing people are different questions. Weighting by population answers the question about people.
